measure: Our own doctrine, not generic best practice. Generic advice is free and worthless.

ideas.observation: We hold both deal-zone room and per-pack economics for the same products.
ideas.suggestion: A "rip or trade" tool could answer one question nobody else can: at today's prices, is this box worth more opened, sold sealed online, or traded at a table? Three numbers we already compute, one screen.

ideas.observation: Print windows and shelf movement are computed separately and never combined.
ideas.suggestion: A late-print set whose shelves are draining is a genuinely different situation from either signal alone. Crossing them is free and nobody publishes it.

ideas.observation: The index has no matched sample today, so it cannot move.
ideas.suggestion: Expected on a fresh series — worth a line on the page saying so, rather than a number that looks stuck.

ideas.observation: The knowledge base holds 8 verified facts.
ideas.suggestion: This is the asset that compounds — instruments can be rebuilt in a weekend, a decade of sourced facts cannot. A steady few per week beats a burst.

ideas.observation: artist-instruments.json is written every run and read by nothing — not another script, not the feed.
ideas.suggestion: Either surface it (the app, the Pulse, a creator tool) or stop generating it. Work that runs daily and reaches nobody is the most expensive kind.

ideas.observation: era-history.json is written every run and read by nothing — not another script, not the feed.
ideas.suggestion: Either surface it (the app, the Pulse, a creator tool) or stop generating it. Work that runs daily and reaches nobody is the most expensive kind.

ideas.observation: date-to-day-key is implemented inline 29 times across the pipeline.
ideas.suggestion: Centralise it — scripts/rotate.mjs already centralises day maths. Repeated maths is where two places drift and only one gets fixed.

ideas.observation: money rounding is implemented inline 9 times across the pipeline.
ideas.suggestion: Centralise it — one helper would make cents behave identically everywhere. Repeated maths is where two places drift and only one gets fixed.

ideas.observation: The daily run imports 30 steps from one file.
ideas.suggestion: Consider grouping them (intake → compute → publish → agents) so the order is legible at a glance. A long flat list is where an ordering mistake hides.
Large files are where two people edit the same function on the same day. Splitting by concern would make collisions rarer and reviews honest.
